title: DeepInfer Automation: What It Is and How to Use It
summary: DeepInfer automation setup requires configuration choices and system limits. You'll complete installation and troubleshoot deployment issues.
body_markdown:
## Passing DeepInfer Output to Other Apps With Activepieces


Results leave DeepInfer by whatever route its documentation lists, a webhook, an API or an export. Activepieces earns a place only when that route needs retries or failure alerts you can't get otherwise.


Check the limits page for that route before the first run. If the docs list none of the three, there's nothing for a workflow tool to attach to, and no tool changes that.


### When a Direct DeepInfer Integration Is Enough


If DeepInfer's documentation names a built-in connection to the app that receives your results, use it. One result goes to one destination, the destination is the system your team already reads, and a missed delivery is something someone would notice and rerun by hand.


Put a middle layer here and you get one more account, one more credential and one more place for a run to fail without anyone seeing it.


Read the connection's documented behavior on failure. If it says nothing about what happens when the destination rejects a result, assume the result is dropped, and test that on day one with a deliberately bad destination.


### When a separate workflow tool earns its place


**Activepieces connects to 747 integrations** , counted from its open-source, MIT-licensed monorepo, so the app receiving your results is likely already covered, and every flow it runs sits under your own RBAC and audit logs. Here it would sit between DeepInfer and everything downstream.


A webhook trigger receives the result when DeepInfer sends one, or an HTTP step calls DeepInfer's API on a schedule if the docs describe that route.


From there the same result can fan out to several destinations, and Activepieces can reshape it to fit each one and retry it when a destination is down.


A failed step can also send an alert to a person, so a dropped result shows up as a message rather than a gap found weeks later.


That's the whole case for it, and it's conditional. You need documented output you can reach, more than one destination or a transformation in between, and a cost to silent failure. If you have only one of those, the direct route is simpler.


If DeepInfer's own limits cut a run short, Activepieces can't recover results that were never produced. It handles what happens after a result exists.
